What was measured

Table 4. What was measured
Comparatorplacebo

Pooled result

Estimate withdrawn. Two of the three trials on this page register only continuous primary outcomes, and this page pooled event counts. Verbatim: STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM each register two co-primaries, 'Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score' and 'Change in Body Weight'. Both are continuous change scores. Neither is an event count and neither can produce a 2x2 table. The counts stored for STEP-HFpEF DM, 7 of 310 against 18 of 306, correspond to no registered primary outcome of that trial. Summit is different and is the only row here with a defensible source: it registers a continuous KCCQ primary and 'First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Heart Failure (HF) Outcomes', and its stored 29 of 364 against 52 of 367 do correspond to that event co-primary. So the pool joins one trial's registered event composite to another trial's unregistered counts. Separately: the outcome name and the measure describe different quantities. The outcome is named 'Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score' and the stored measure is an odds ratio. A change score has no odds. Separately again, and it is why this topic was invisible: this page had no index card at all. It is linked from the index table and appears in no card, so it published a pooled odds ratio of 0.4846 (0.3178 to 0.7389) that the corpus's own card-alignment checking could never reach -- there was no card to compare against the page.

What this does not establish: not that incretin therapies do not help in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. STEP-HFpEF, STEP-HFpEF DM and summit all report benefit on the outcomes they were designed around -- symptom burden measured by KCCQ, and body weight -- and summit additionally reports its heart-failure event composite. The trials here measure symptom scores and weight, and nothing on this page estimated those. What is confirmed: summit's stored counts ARE its registered event co-primary, and all three identities are correct. The replacement question is available and parked: all three trials share a KCCQ clinical-summary-score primary, so a mean difference synthesis of symptom benefit is squarely defensible and needs no estimand judgement -- only each trial's least-squares mean difference read from its results record. That is the second such case in this programme, after BOCOCIZUMAB_LIPID.

Registered as continuous in two trials -- and pooled here as an event count. k = 2.

A published synthesis of this question included 4 trials where this pool carries 2. Source: Musa & Musa, BMC Cardiovascular Disorders 2026, PMID 41906074, a prospectively registered systematic review (CRD420251237462).

Which trials are ABSENT is not established. The published abstract names none of its included studies and no included-study table was read, so this is a difference in stated counts and nothing more. It is not a claim that 2 specific trials were missed, and nobody here has identified them.

The estimate above is computed from the trials this object carries and is not withdrawn or altered by this note. What a reader is owed is the scope: a larger evidence base on this question exists in the literature, and whether this review's search should be widened is a decision that has not been made.

MD 7.43 (5.09 to 9.77), 95% interval

Change in KCCQ clinical summary score. random-effects, estimator REML random-effects, inverse-variance (tau-squared estimated as zero), k = 2.

τ² not stated · I² 0% · Q 0.1375 on 1 df

Favours: the intervention (lower is better)

Q = 0.1375 on 1 df, I-squared 0 per cent. At k=2 that means the two trials agree, not that the finding generalises.

This is a replacement, not a correction. The withdrawn estimate on this page was an odds ratio over event counts, and two of the three included trials register only continuous co-primaries. But all three register the same continuous outcome -- change in the KCCQ clinical summary score -- so a symptom-benefit analysis needs no estimand judgement at all. It is pooled at k=2, not k=3, and that is the honest number. STEP-HFpEF DM's ClinicalTrials.gov record carries no results section, so this project has no registry-sourced value for it. Its published KCCQ difference exists in the literature and is not used here, because every value on this page is read from a registry results record and importing one from elsewhere would break that guarantee for the sake of a third data point. The two values are the registry's own: step-HFpEF 7.8 (4.8 to 10.9) over 243 against 237, and summit 6.9 (3.3 to 10.6) over 301 against 313. Pooled: MD 7.43 (5.09 to 9.77) points on the KCCQ clinical summary score, k=2, 1,094 participants. Q = 0.14 on 1 degree of freedom, I-squared 0 per cent -- the two trials agree almost exactly.

Why this pool stands. This is a replacement, not a correction. The withdrawn estimate on this page was an odds ratio over event counts, and two of the three included trials register only continuous co-primaries. But all three register the same continuous outcome -- change in the KCCQ clinical summary score -- so a symptom-benefit analysis needs no estimand judgement at all. It is pooled at k=2, not k=3, and that is the honest number. STEP-HFpEF DM's ClinicalTrials.gov record carries no results section, so this project has no registry-sourced value for it. Its published KCCQ difference exists in the literature and is not used here, because every value on this page is read from a registry results record and importing one from elsewhere would break that guarantee for the sake of a third data point. The two values are the registry's own: step-HFpEF 7.8 (4.8 to 10.9) over 243 against 237, and summit 6.9 (3.3 to 10.6) over 301 against 313. Pooled: MD 7.43 (5.09 to 9.77) points on the KCCQ clinical summary score, k=2, 1,094 participants. Q = 0.14 on 1 degree of freedom, I-squared 0 per cent -- the two trials agree almost exactly.

What a reader should know. (1) k=2 and the interval shown is the wald one. At two studies a Hartung-Knapp interval uses a t-distribution on one degree of freedom. This project's interval is -7.74 TO 22.60 and it includes no effect. An earlier version of this sentence gave 1.80 to 13.06 and said the interval still excluded no effect; those figures are metafor's raw unfloored knha output, not this project's, and the conclusion drawn from them was wrong. The raw inflation factor here is 0.3708, so the unfloored adjustment narrows rather than widens -- the instability the house floor exists to prevent. Both are recorded. (2) heterogeneity is zero here, which at k=2 means the two trials agree, not that the finding is general. (3) the third trial is missing for a provenance reason, not a clinical one. STEP-HFpEF DM would very likely move this estimate very little; it is left out because its registry record has no results, and that is a rule about where numbers may come from rather than a judgement about the trial. (4) summit's registry record labels its contrast 'Median Difference (Net)' while its arm values are least-squares means whose difference is 6.83. The label and the quantity disagree in the registry. The reported value is used and the discrepancy is stated rather than resolved. (5) a seven-point KCCQ difference is a symptom benefit, not an event reduction. Five points is the usual threshold for a clinically meaningful within-patient change. Nothing here estimates an effect on death or hospitalisation -- summit registers a heart-failure event co-primary and this analysis does not use it.

Correction, and it reverses what this page said about its own sensitivity analysis. The caveat on this pool stated that the Hartung-Knapp interval 'gives 1.80 to 13.06 -- far wider, and arguably the honest interval at this k. It still excludes no effect.' the figures 1.80 TO 13.06 ARE metafor's raw unfloored knha output. This project's interval is -7.7429 TO 22.6028, and it includes no effect.

The raw variance-inflation factor on this pool is 0.3708 -- metafor's Hartung-Knapp standard error is barely a third of the random-effects one -- so the unfloored adjustment narrows the interval instead of widening it. That is the exact instability this project's floor exists to prevent, and it is why the raw figures looked reassuringly wide next to the Wald interval while being the product of a correction pointing the wrong way.

The point estimate and its wald interval are unchanged: MD 7.43 (5.09 to 9.77) points on the KCCQ clinical summary score, k = 2, 1,094 participants. What changes is a sentence about what the sensitivity analysis showed, which said the opposite of what it shows. A seven-point KCCQ difference remains a symptom benefit and this page still estimates nothing about death or hospitalisation.

  2. Read this beside `whether the estimand was established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the same quantity. It records nothing about what that quantity was measured against -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.
  3. No GRADE assessment or reconciliation record is held in this object, so the certainty of this evidence has not been rated. This is recorded as a declared departure under Cochrane Handbook §III.3.4.1: the review reports a pooled estimate for which no certainty assessment was made. Rating it here would require two assessors and an adjudicator, and a rating produced by neither is not a GRADE assessment whatever letter it carries.

Components as the registry states thema continuous KCCQ primary and 'First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Heart Failure (HF) Outcomes'. The 29 and 52 stored here DO correspond to that event co-primary.
Components as the registry states themKCCQ clinical summary score, change from baseline. A continuous symptom measure, higher is better.
Analysis set as the registry states itAs registered by each trial. STEP-HFpEF reports an 'Estimated Treatment Difference'; Summit's registry record labels its contrast 'Median Difference (Net)' while its arm values are least-squares means (19.51 against 12.68, a difference of 6.83) -- the label and the quantity do not match in that record, and the value used here is the one the registry reports.
A a published synthesis carried more trials than this poolA published synthesis of this question included 4 trials where this pool carries 2. Source: Musa & Musa, BMC Cardiovascular Disorders 2026, PMID 41906074, a prospectively registered systematic review (CRD420251237462).
B whether the extra trials can be namedWhich trials are ABSENT is not established. The published abstract names none of its included studies and no included-study table was read, so this is a difference in stated counts and nothing more. It is not a claim that 2 specific trials were missed, and nobody here has identified them.
C what this means for the estimate aboveThe estimate above is computed from the trials this object carries and is not withdrawn or altered by this note. What a reader is owed is the scope: a larger evidence base on this question exists in the literature, and whether this review's search should be widened is a decision that has not been made.
CaveatsWhat a reader should know. (1) k=2 and the interval shown is the wald one. At two studies a Hartung-Knapp interval uses a t-distribution on one degree of freedom. This project's interval is -7.74 TO 22.60 and it includes no effect. An earlier version of this sentence gave 1.80 to 13.06 and said the interval still excluded no effect; those figures are metafor's raw unfloored knha output, not this project's, and the conclusion drawn from them was wrong. The raw inflation factor here is 0.3708, so the unfloored adjustment narrows rather than widens -- the instability the house floor exists to prevent. Both are recorded. (2) heterogeneity is zero here, which at k=2 means the two trials agree, not that the finding is general. (3) the third trial is missing for a provenance reason, not a clinical one. STEP-HFpEF DM would very likely move this estimate very little; it is left out because its registry record has no results, and that is a rule about where numbers may come from rather than a judgement about the trial. (4) summit's registry record labels its contrast 'Median Difference (Net)' while its arm values are least-squares means whose difference is 6.83. The label and the quantity disagree in the registry. The reported value is used and the discrepancy is stated rather than resolved. (5) a seven-point KCCQ difference is a symptom benefit, not an event reduction. Five points is the usual threshold for a clinically meaningful within-patient change. Nothing here estimates an effect on death or hospitalisation -- summit registers a heart-failure event co-primary and this analysis does not use it.
Why the earlier refusal does not carryThis figure was refused earlier, on the ground that every number in this object was registry-sourced and breaking that for one data point costs the guarantee that makes the rest checkable. That reasoning was about an unsourced import. The source is now identified, quotable and tiered, and the mixed provenance is declared per trial rather than hidden. The refusal was right about an unsourced number and does not extend to a sourced one.
What this does not establishNot that the two trials are free of bias -- no RoB-2 assessment is recorded. Not that tirzepatide and semaglutide are interchangeable: this pools two different incretin agents against placebo on one instrument, which is a decision about the question being asked and is visible on the face of the topic. Not that the abstract figure equals the full-text table figure.
Why the test is the title and not the disclosureDisclosure does not make an incoherent pool coherent. Four cardiology topics closed on exactly this point -- not whether the combination was disclosed, but whether the question the page asks is the question the pool answers. Had this been titled for one agent, declaring the second would not have fixed it; the title would have had to change, as azilsartan's did.
What the pool does not establish about the classIt does not establish that the class is homogeneous. I-squared is 0% and tau-squared is zero, and AT k=2 that is weak evidence of agreement rather than strong evidence of it: with two studies a heterogeneity statistic cannot distinguish genuine similarity from insufficient data to detect a difference. The two point estimates (6.83 and 7.30) are close, which is consistent with a class effect and does not demonstrate one. A reader should take this as a class-level estimate of two agents, not as evidence that incretins behave alike on this instrument.
What it does do for our identity checkThe registration identity was previously checked in one direction only -- from the registry to the trial -- because the nejm paper could not be opened. This paper prints, in its own abstract, that STEP-HFpEF DM is registered as NCT04916470. That is an independent published source tying the trial name to the registration, which strengthens the identity materially. It is still not the check that was wanted: it does not establish which NCT is printed on the nejm paper the 7.3-point figure was quoted . That remains unverified.
What this comparison does not establishNot that our pooled KCCQ estimate is right or wrong -- their paper does not report the quantity we pool. Not that semaglutide and tirzepatide behave alike on heart-failure events; their analysis contains no tirzepatide. Not that a symptom-score benefit implies an event benefit, or the reverse: that inference is not licensed by either synthesis and neither paper claims it.
A the sensitivity interval this page quoted was not this project sCorrection, and it reverses what this page said about its own sensitivity analysis. The caveat on this pool stated that the Hartung-Knapp interval 'gives 1.80 to 13.06 -- far wider, and arguably the honest interval at this k. It still excludes no effect.' the figures 1.80 TO 13.06 ARE metafor's raw unfloored knha output. This project's interval is -7.7429 TO 22.6028, and it includes no effect.
B why the raw interval is the wrong one here specificallyThe raw variance-inflation factor on this pool is 0.3708 -- metafor's Hartung-Knapp standard error is barely a third of the random-effects one -- so the unfloored adjustment narrows the interval instead of widening it. That is the exact instability this project's floor exists to prevent, and it is why the raw figures looked reassuringly wide next to the Wald interval while being the product of a correction pointing the wrong way.
Scopeprimary: first heart-failure hospitalisation. Secondary: KCCQ clinical summary score, six-minute walk distance, weight, all-cause mortality.
The finding of this comparisonThey pooled where we declined, which is the opposite of class 76. This topic was named in advance as a predicted class-76 instance on the grounds that it pools two different drugs -- semaglutide and tirzepatide. The published synthesis pools that same class mix across more trials, in a prospectively registered review, and pools the first-heart-failure-hospitalisation outcome that this object declares primary and leaves unpooled. The prediction was wrong and is recorded as wrong. Whether this object should pool its primary is a content decision and is not made here.
What this review does not publishWhat this review does not publish. This review also examined one outcome for which no pooled estimate is published: Registered as continuous in two trials -- and pooled here as an event count (k=2) -- two of the three trials on this page register only continuous primary outcomes, and this P. Each of those outcomes is recorded on this review with the reason it was not pooled, and none of them contributes to the estimate reported above (7.43 at k=2). A reader meeting the pooled result should not take it as covering every outcome, or every trial, this review examined. This sentence exists because a second, independent reading -- by a different model family, given the object and the abstract and none of our conclusions -- found that a reader would reasonably conclude the review pools all relevant trials, and that the object does not support that. The withdrawals were already recorded beside the outcomes they concern; they were invisible from the abstract, which is where the impression forms.

Each statement below cites the record it came from; those sources are listed at the end of every section. Where the record holds nothing, the section says so by name rather than being left out, so a procedure that was not carried out can be told from one that simply was never mentioned.

Title

Incretin therapies in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction1

This object contradicts itself about which semaglutide trial contributed. `inputs.trials` names NCT04916470; the pooled outcome `KCCQ css change` carries NCT04788511. These are different trials. Read from ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 2026-08-21: NCT04788511 is STEP-HFpEF, registered condition 'Obesity'; NCT04916470 is STEP HFpEF DM, registered condition 'Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF) and Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2'. One enrols people with diabetes and the other excludes them. Which of the two supplied the pooled value is not decidable from what this object holds, and it is not guessed here. It is recorded so that a reader is not shown a trial list that disagrees with the trials behind the number, and so the next pass resolves it against the source the value was read from rather than by picking one.2

Results

The pooled mean difference for change in KCCQ clinical summary score was 7.43 (5.09 to 9.77) across 2 trials, against placebo.1

Noted on this pool. Correction, and it reverses what this page said about its own sensitivity analysis. The caveat on this pool stated that the Hartung-Knapp interval 'gives 1.80 to 13.06 -- far wider, and arguably the honest interval at this k. It still excludes no effect.' the figures 1.80 TO 13.06 ARE metafor's raw unfloored knha output. This project's interval is -7.7429 TO 22.6028, and it includes no effect. The raw variance-inflation factor on this pool is 0.3708 -- metafor's Hartung-Knapp standard error is barely a third of the random-effects one -- so the unfloored adjustment narrows the interval instead of widening it. That is the exact instability this project's floor exists to prevent, and it is why the raw figures looked reassuringly wide next to the Wald interval while being the product of a correction pointing the wrong way. The point estimate and its wald interval are unchanged: MD 7.43 (5.09 to 9.77) points on the KCCQ clinical summary score, k = 2, 1,094 participants. What changes is a sentence about what the sensitivity analysis showed, which said the opposite of what it shows. A seven-point KCCQ difference remains a symptom benefit and this page still estimates nothing about death or hospitalisation.2

The trials' results were closely consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 0%; the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 0.138, on degrees of freedom 1. Q = 0.1375 on 1 df, I-squared 0 per cent. At k=2 that means the two trials agree, not that the finding generalises.3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: This is a replacement, not a correction. The withdrawn estimate on this page was an odds ratio over event counts, and two of the three included trials register only continuous co-primaries. But all three register the same continuous outcome -- change in the KCCQ clinical summary score -- so a symptom-benefit analysis needs no estimand judgement at all. It is pooled at k=2, not k=3, and that is the honest number. STEP-HFpEF DM's ClinicalTrials.gov record carries no results section, so this project has no registry-sourced value for it. Its published KCCQ difference exists in the literature and is not used here, because every value on this page is read from a registry results record and importing one from elsewhere would break that guarantee for the sake of a third data point. The two values are the registry's own: step-HFpEF 7.8 (4.8 to 10.9) over 243 against 237, and summit 6.9 (3.3 to 10.6) over 301 against 313. Pooled: MD 7.43 (5.09 to 9.77) points on the KCCQ clinical summary score, k=2, 1,094 participants. Q = 0.14 on 1 degree of freedom, I-squared 0 per cent -- the two trials agree almost exactly. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

Registered as continuous in two trials -- and pooled here as an event count. These 2 trials are not pooled, and the reason is stated rather than the outcome being quietly omitted: Two of the three trials on this page register only continuous primary outcomes, and this page pooled event counts. Verbatim: STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM each register two co-primaries, 'Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score' and 'Change in Body Weight'. Both are continuous change scores. Neither is an event count and neither can produce a 2x2 table. The counts stored for STEP-HFpEF DM, 7 of 310 against 18 of 306, correspond to no registered primary outcome of that trial. Summit is different and is the only row here with a defensible source: it registers a continuous KCCQ primary and 'First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Heart Failure (HF) Outcomes', and its stored 29 of 364 against 52 of 367 do correspond to that event co-primary. So the pool joins one trial's registered event composite to another trial's unregistered counts. Separately: the outcome name and the measure describe different quantities. The outcome is named 'Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score' and the stored measure is an odds ratio. A change score has no odds. Separately again, and it is why this topic was invisible: this page's card was invisible to our own tooling. The card existed and published 'HR 0.41 (0.22 to 0.79), k=3' -- a measure, a value and a trial count that all differ from the object's OR 0.4846 (0.3178 to 0.7389) at k=2. It was reported as having no card because two scripts matched card links with the pattern [A-Z0-9_]+\.html, which cannot match the lowercase 'p' in HFpEF. A page invisible to the tool that counts pages is worse than an uncounted one: it is counted as a different thing, and this card escaped card-alignment checking entirely for as long as those tools have run. And, recorded separately on the withdrawal itself: two of the three trials on this page register only continuous primary outcomes, and this page pooled event counts. Both are continuous change scores. Neither is an event count and neither can produce a 2x2 table. So the pool joins one trial's registered event composite to another trial's unregistered counts. Separately: the outcome name and the measure describe different quantities. The outcome is named 'Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score' and the stored measure is an odds ratio. A change score has no odds. Separately again, and it is why this topic was invisible: this page had no index card at all. It is linked from the index table and appears in no card, so it published a pooled odds ratio of 0.4846 (0.3178 to 0.7389) that the corpus's own card-alignment checking could never reach -- there was no card to compare against the page.5

Limitations

Eligible trials that do not contribute: STEP-HFpEF dm is excluded from the replacement for a provenance reason, not a clinical one. Its ClinicalTrials.gov record carries no results section, so no registry-sourced KCCQ difference exists for it. Its published value exists in the literature and is deliberately not imported: every number on this page is read from a registry results record, and breaking that for one extra data point would cost the guarantee that makes the rest checkable.1

This review does not claim that any per-trial count was checked against a results record.2

1 claim(s) previously made about this review were corrected and the corrections are retained on the object rather than overwritten.3

What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm, any absolute effect or number needed to treat and any measure of harm. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.4
